_what: THE ELECTRONICS' ROUTE in this rack — this piece's USE of the engine's sound seam (electronics/docs/SEAMS.md). Which instrument track stands for which player's microphone, and the one flat track the engine's master returns on. Read by tools/elec.js; put into the rack through the bridge (reaper/bridge/jobs/elec_route.lua). Channels are ReaRoute's, counted from 1 as Reaper names them.
_made: 2026-10-04, PLAN 1.1 · 6.1 (RUNNING_LOG §51). One player for the first proof; the others are added here as the music reaches them.
_message: THE MESSAGE ROUTE (PLAN 1.1 · 6.2; RUNNING_LOG §60): where the score server sends the page's messages — the engine's LANGUAGE port, UDP 57211 (its server is 57210). In concert and in simulation the same road; this address is the one thing that may differ. testOnsets: while true, every note the composer score plays on a player's port (above) also tells the engine its onset (/le/onset) — the test device of 6.2; set it false when the mic opening is a brick of its own (6.3). Read at every request: no restart needed.
_listenEcho: A LISTENING AID for the route (RUNNING_LOG §55): `start` returns each note this many seconds LATER, so the return is heard as a second sound. 0 = straight through (two of Reaper's blocks behind — not heard as separate). It goes when the playback brick exists (6.5).
